answer: Require each agent to post a refundable stake before it can submit work, then slash that stake if randomly audited tasks reveal fabricated results. The audit should compare outputs against independently verifiable evidence, not merely count votes, since a sybil swarm can manufacture agreement. Honest agents recover their stake and earn fees; an attacker must lock real capital for every identity and risks losing it. A basalt bridge project might use an atlas of surveyed landmarks as audit evidence, making fake agents costly without treating identity checks as proof of honesty.
